lots.title: Multi-disciplinary Design Team Appointment — Stockport Town Centre School
lots.description: Appointment of an architecturally led multi-disciplinary design team (Architect, MEP, Structures & Civils) by Metropolitan Borough Council of Stockport to develop a feasibility through to concept design of a new school in a town centre location, under a Terms of Appointment agreement with optional novation to a design-and-build contractor (Schedule 6). This document is the terms and conditions template governing the appointment; it does not subdivide the scope into separately bidable lots.
requirements: Exercise the reasonable skill, care and diligence of a professional consultant of the relevant discipline experienced in projects of similar nature, size and complexity (clause 2.2).

Do not specify, approve or authorise materials contravening any British or EU Standard or Code of Practice, known to be deleterious, or inconsistent with 'Good Practice in the Selection of Construction Materials' (British Council of Offices) and the BRE Digest current at date of specification (clause 2.3).
Comply with all Statutory Requirements and obtain Requisite Consents (clause 5.2).
Act as a 'designer' under the CDM Regulations 2015, allocate adequate resources and competence, and cooperate with the Principal Designer (clause 20).
Maintain professional indemnity insurance of not less than £10,000,000 for any one claim in any one period of insurance (Schedule 1, clause 7).
Accept overall limitation of Consultant liability capped at £10,000,000 for any one claim (Schedule 1, clause 23.3).
Comply with Public Contracts Regulations 2015, including cascading regulations 57, 71 and 113 into sub-contracts (clause 8.5).

Comply with Bribery Act 2010 (clause 17), Modern Slavery Act 2015 (clause 18), Equality Act 2010 (clause 19), Freedom of Information Act 2000 / Environmental Information Regulations 2004 (clause 14) and GDPR / Data Protection Act 2018 as data processor (clause 25).
Execute collateral warranties (Schedules 4 and 5) and a Deed of Novation (Schedule 6) within 28 days of engrossments when required (clause 9.5–9.7).
Provide key personnel on a full-time basis as named in the Contract Particulars and replace staff at the Client's reasonable request (clause 16).

Submit interim invoices at intervals of not less than one month; payment due 21 days after receipt; final date for payment 30 days; interest at Bank of England base rate +5% applies on late payment (clause 4).
Notify any Claim in writing within 10 Working Days of the triggering event as a condition precedent to entitlement (clauses 4.14–4.15).
